latest_news.head: Copilot 9/30 status check: the 10/1 prepaid seat change is one day out and the 10/22 default-policy window is 22 days out.
latest_news.detail: Assigned seats move to prepaid billing at the start of each billing cycle from 10/1: idle seats are charged the same as active ones and removing a seat does not produce a refund, and new customers must pay before provisioning. From 10/22, GitHub's Default policy for new features takes effect, under which any GA feature or supported client capability still sitting in Unconfigured inherits the administrator's chosen default, falling back to GitHub's own default of Enabled if the administrator never chose. The scope covers the enterprise Features and clients page, the Agents page Copilot Code Review policy and the MCP page MCP servers policy. Out of scope and therefore always default-disabled are pre-GA models, open-weight models (DeepSeek, Kimi K2.7 Code, Kimi K3) and models not covered by GitHub's data retention agreement (Claude Fable 5 and Fable 5.1).

latest_news.head: Head-to-head: Baidu Qianfan Token Plan vs Xiaomi MiMo Token Plan. They are not the same product, and the value gap swings 13x depending on model choice and cache behaviour.
latest_news.detail: Both vendors refreshed on the same day. Qianfan shipped a credit-plan mode alongside its existing Token-plan plus an all-hours tiered discount (GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813: 2-off weekday daytime, 0.5-off weekday nights, 1-off all weekend, quota magnified up to 20x) and a National-Day pack running 9/24-10/7. Xiaomi moved its Token Plan to the V2.6 generation at unchanged prices and quotas, added a team plan at 99/329/659 CNY per seat per month with a two-seat minimum, and set 10/21 10:00 Beijing time as the sunset for mimo-v2.5-pro and mimo-v2.5. The structural difference is in what the metering unit is worth. Qianfan's Token-plan deducts one token per token with no distinction between model multiplier, input/output or cache hit, which flattens model multipliers: on a CNY 40 Lite tier covering 42M tokens, running GLM-5.3 at 50,000 uncached input plus 500 output per round yields 832 rounds worth about CNY 207 of API-equivalent spend, a 5.16x multiple; the same plan on a 90-percent-cache workload still yields 832 rounds because Token-plan does not reward caching, worth CNY 72 or 1.80x; but switching to the cheap deepseek-v4.1-flash on the cached workload yields only CNY 16 of face value, a 0.40x multiple that is an actual loss. Xiaomi instead pegs its credit 1:1 to its own API rates (1 credit equals CNY 1e-8, cross-validated against both mimo-v2.6-pro at 300 credits per uncached input token equalling CNY 3 per MTok and mimo-v2.6-flash at 100 credits equalling CNY 1 per MTok), so each tier carries a fixed face value of 41/110/380/820 CNY against a price of 39/99/329/659 CNY, a value multiple of 1.05x to 1.24x that never varies. On the same CNY 39-40 Lite tier, Xiaomi's v2.6-pro delivers 268 rounds on the uncached workload and 2,144 rounds on the cached one, while v2.6-flash delivers 804 and 5,942 rounds respectively. So Qianfan wins by roughly 5x on flagship models with low cache reuse and by roughly 1.7x on flagship models with heavy caching, but loses by roughly 2.6x when cheap models are used with heavy caching, and wins overwhelmingly once the night-window discount is applied, where a CNY 40 Lite plan running DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 overnight is equivalent to 840 million tokens. Other decisive differences: Xiaomi states outright that there is no 5-hour and no weekly cap whereas Qianfan's equivalent caps are only temporarily lifted, so the policy risk sits with Qianfan; Qianfan offers third-party flagships (GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi) plus an enterprise seat plan while Xiaomi offers only its own eight MiMo models but adds native image, video and audio input, ASR at 30M credits per hour and free TTS; both ban non-coding use of the plan key, both refuse refunds, and Qianfan additionally limits one plan per account with no downgrade.

latest_news.head: Baidu Qianfan re-verified: Token-plan mode and credit-plan mode are NOT the same thing - the tier quota table implies a break-even exchange rate of 4,242 to 7,143 tokens per credit, and the official worked example lands only 10.5% away from that point.
latest_news.detail: Qianfan is the only vendor in the tracked set running two parallel billing modes on the same subscription, and they are routinely mistaken for the same thing. Official definitions: token mode deducts 'the actual number of tokens consumed, without distinguishing input, output or cached tokens'; credit mode sets 'separate deduction coefficients for input, output and cached tokens' and pools different models behind a single credit balance. The quota table itself encodes the break-even rate, since token quota divided by credit quota tells you how many tokens one credit must buy to be equivalent: Mini 7,143 / Lite 6,364 / Pro 5,111 / Max 4,242 tokens per credit - so the higher the tier, the more generous credit mode becomes relative to token mode. The official worked example (853 input + 10,240 cached + 427 output = 11,520 tokens for 3 credits, i.e. 3,840 tokens per credit) sits only about 10.5% below the Max-tier threshold, which is exactly why the two tracks feel interchangeable: they are calibrated against a high-cache agent workload. Move away from that point and the gap widens quickly - with no cache hits token mode is roughly 5.0x cheaper (845 tokens per credit), while at a 96%-99% cache share credit mode wins by 1.6x-2.0x. Credit mode only overtakes above a cache-hit share of roughly 86.1% (Max), 89.8% (Pro), 93.4% (Lite) and 95.0% (Mini) of total tokens, so the bar is lower on the expensive tiers. Cheaper models pull in the other direction: if a model's coefficients scale with its price, a model priced around 8x below the flagship already makes credit mode win even with zero cache hits, and at an 89% cache share by about 8x. Baidu does NOT publish individual-edition credit coefficients, so that sensitivity is a proportional estimate rather than an official number. Three hard constraints matter far more than any discount. First, migration is one-way: Token to Credit is supported and pro-rated by remaining balance (a 20% token balance becomes 20% of the credit quota), while Credit to Token is explicitly unsupported - so the risk-minimising default is to start on token mode and keep the option to switch. Second, the 5-hour and 7-day usage caps are attached to credit mode only and are currently suspended on a limited-time basis, while no such clause exists for token mode - the policy-risk exposure is on the credit side. Third, the 7-day reset card is issued to credit-mode users only. The all-hours tiered discount and the National-Day pack apply to both tracks (official wording: credit OR token quota amplified up to 20x) and therefore do not decide the track. Practical rule: run flagship models such as GLM-5.3, GLM-5.2 or DeepSeek-V4-Pro with a modest cache-hit rate and token mode wins; run Flash-class models, or sustain cache hits above roughly 90% of total tokens, and credit mode wins.

latest_news.head: Anthropic IPO prospectus draft exposed by Reuters: 261 pages, $518B compute obligations, target valuation above $2T
latest_news.detail: 2025 revenue grew 12x to just under $4.6B against a $42.0B net loss (about $34B non-cash convertible fair-value charge; operating loss $8.06B excluding it, up from $2.98B in 2024). Compute and infrastructure spend of $7.33B was more than half of $12.65B total operating expense, and $518B of cloud/compute purchase obligations are stated for the coming years - the stated core motivation for the raise. Cash and short-term investments of $20.28B at year-end. Target valuation above $2T versus the company own $965B May mark; listing likely pushed beyond November. The 80-page risk section warns models may resist shutdown, conceal or manipulate information and behave in blackmail-like ways, and nearly a quarter of 2025 revenue came from two customers with no long-term lock-in.

latest_news.head: Claude Sonnet 5.5 ships at Sonnet 5 pricing and jumps Terminal-Bench 4.0 to 70.6%, above Opus 5.5
latest_news.detail: Corrects the 9/28 morning call that Sonnet 5.5 was a debunked rumour. Priced unchanged at $2 in / $10 out with cache read $0.20 and cache write $2.50; Anthropic claims >30% faster output and up to 30% lower cost per task from fewer tokens, tool calls and steps. Terminal-Bench 4.0 70.6% versus Sonnet 5 10.3% and Opus 5.5 66.4% at xhigh; GDPval-AA v2.1 1,844 against 1,846 for Opus 5.5. Model id claude-sonnet-5-5 on Claude, AWS, Google Cloud and Azure with zero data retention; Claude Code 2.1.284 makes it the default Sonnet. Disabled-thinking requests return 400, and an independent test put max-effort cost at $7.60 per task versus Opus 5.5 at $5.98.

latest_news.head: MiniMax announces M Plan to succeed Token Plan, with Token Plan closing to new purchases
latest_news.detail: Pricing and text usage quotas unchanged, and select tiers unlock the full MiniMax lineup including H3 (currently excluded). Existing subscribers with auto-renewal on keep their plan and benefits; turning auto-renewal off or interrupting it means the existing Token Plan can no longer be purchased. Upgrading to M Plan forfeits Token Plan legacy perks such as unlimited quota and 150% weekly quota. Perks include unlimited M3.1-Flash-Preview in MiniMax Code from 10/01 to 10/07, 50% off the first month through 10/14 and bonus credits at launch. Everything requires MiniMax Code v3.1.0, still unreleased as of 9/29.

latest_news.head: OpenAI $200 Pro reopens with about half the API-equivalent allowance; the 10/30 cutoff is now dated
latest_news.detail: Tibo Sottiaux says the new Pro $200 nets out at about half the dollar API spend of the old plan. Existing subscribers keep current limits through 10/29, then Work/Codex falls from 20x to 10x Plus and GPT-6 Pro in Chat from 200 to 100 messages per week, with a one-time 62,500 usage credit grant OpenAI values at $2,500 expiring 2026-12-31. OpenAI commits not to reintroduce the 5-hour window. Pro 500 at $500/month carries 25x Plus and is the only individual tier with Astra Ultrafast, which consumes 8x the plan allowance (Fast mode 2.5x).

latest_news.head: GitHub Copilot ships Claude Sonnet 5.5 (9/28) and GPT-6.1 Sol (9/29), both default-enabled and billed at list price
latest_news.detail: Sonnet 5.5 goes to Pro and above, Sol to Pro+ / Max / Business / Enterprise. GitHub early testing found Sonnet 5.5 matching Sonnet 5 on coding tasks with significantly fewer steps, tokens and tool calls, and Sol using fewer tokens and steps than GPT-6 or GPT-5.6. Both are billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing and both are enabled by default under the default model enablement policy, so administrators must use the model policy to gate them. First real test of the 9/28 unpriced-default regime.

latest_news.head: Claude Code Cloud Sessions reach general availability with $100 / $250 promotional credits
latest_news.detail: Cloud sessions run on Anthropic-hosted infrastructure and continue after the local machine disconnects; launch surfaces include claude.ai/code, the mobile Code section, the desktop app and claude --cloud. Pro subscribers get $100 and Max subscribers $250 in promotional credits tracked separately from plan allowances and drawn down automatically during cloud sessions; claim by 10/07 and spend before 11/04, after which usage reverts to the standard plan allowance with no separate container charge. Eligibility is limited to individual Pro/Max subscribers active when the promotion began on 2026-09-23.

latest_news.head: Tianyi Cloud adds a Starry Sky TokenHub coding Token Plan at CNY 29 / 89 / 199 and the carrier token landscape fills out
latest_news.detail: 25M / 80M / 180M tokens per month covering GLM-5 official release and DeepSeek-V3.2 flagship, compatible with OpenClaw and Claude Code, metered per thousand tokens with input, output and cache-hit split and hourly billing, deducted free quota first then token packs then pay-as-you-go. China Telecom frames the strategy as rebuilding the business around Token operations with the Tianyi Token coin and trials consumer packages at CNY 9.9-49.9 and developer packages at CNY 39.9-299.9; China Mobile offers packages from CNY 5/month plus CNY 1 for 400,000 tokens in several regions; China Unicom runs Coding plus Token plus bundled plans. All three listed on the China Computing Power Platform compute supermarket since June 2026.

latest_news.head: Alibaba Bailian September campaign closes at 24:00 Beijing time
latest_news.detail: First-payment credit doubling for individual Professional and Advanced tiers issued as Qwen-exclusive credits that cannot be mixed with general credits, plus 1,000 Qwen-exclusive credits for renewal, upgrade or reopening in September once per person on monthly billing. Determined by order payment success time, excluding team edition, enterprise standard, enterprise dedicated and membership cards, with refunded orders still counting as prior payment. AI Renewal Season coupons (CNY 10 off 20, 15 off 99, 35 off 199, 14-day validity) apply to Token Plan and Qoder; Qoder CN offers 100 free credits per day in the same window.

latest_news.head: Windsurf brand folded into Devin: pricing page redirects and the standalone pricing surface is gone
latest_news.detail: As of 2026-09-26 windsurf.com/pricing permanently redirects to devin.ai/pricing and Windsurf is not named on the destination page, while Devin Free advertises unlimited inline edits and Tab completions - the Windsurf editor hallmarks. Current Devin pricing: Free $0, Pro $20, Max $200, Teams $80/month flat plus $40/month per full developer seat up to 200 users, Enterprise on quote, overage at API pricing, SWE-2 free in Devin Desktop and CLI through 2026-10-10. Whether Windsurf continues as a separately sold product is not officially confirmed.

latest_news.head: Z.ai GLM Coding Plan discount and metering structure re-verified
latest_news.detail: Yearly billing takes 30% off (Lite about $12.60, Pro $56, Max $117.60 per month), quarterly 20% off and team seats 10% off annually with a two-seat minimum. Weekly credits: Lite 10,000, Pro 60,000, Max 140,000; team Standard 66,000 and Premium 155,000. Individual subscriptions are limited to the subscriber own interactive coding use, with automated services, resale, shared keys and general API applications out of scope. The older third-party prompt-count framing coexists and should not be used for procurement.

latest_news.head: DeepSeek V4.1 Pro reported to be in per-account grayscale testing with no official release date
latest_news.detail: Reported state is early access with default reasoning effort at High and persistent access once granted, but most users see no entry. DeepSeek Harness 0.2.0 was announced for early this week with the first official desktop-edition confirmation, though DSH lead Cui Tianyi denied a joint release. Consistent with the 9/27 OrcaRouter finding of no official trace: grayscale testing is controlled and the model still appears in no official model list, pricing page or Hugging Face repository.

latest_news.head: Claude Haiku 5.5 ships with two-band pricing - and the 90% cut is really about 75%
latest_news.detail: At or below a 100K prompt $0.10 in / $0.50 out / $0.01 cache read / $0.125 cache write; above 100K it jumps to $0.50 / $2.50 / $0.05 / $0.625. That is 90% and 50% below Haiku 4.5 at the headline band, and exactly the same price as GPT-6 Luna. Anthropic's own measurement puts the average saving at about 75% because roughly 90% of legacy requests sit in the low band and the new tokenizer adds a few tokens - budget on 75%, not 90%. 1M context, first Haiku with adjustable effort. GDPval-AA v2.1 1620, OSWorld 2.1 offline 72.4%, Terminal-Bench 4.0 39.2% at max effort but only about 20% at the default medium effort.

latest_news.head: Anthropic halves Sonnet 5.5 cache reads and adds monthly API allowances to Max/Team
latest_news.detail: Sonnet 5.5 cache reads drop permanently from $0.20 to $0.10 per MTok while input and output stay at $2/$10. Max and Team gain monthly API allowances of $100 / $200 and up to $500 pooled, which cannot be spent on interactive Claude Code and expire at the end of each cycle. computer-use and browser-use SDK betas also landed. Read together with the Haiku 5.5 launch this is a caching-and-agent play, not a price cut on the main line.

latest_news.head: Microsoft says Copilot local model calls will not be billed as inference
latest_news.detail: Copilot gets local model inference before the end of October with automatic orchestration or forced-local modes; local model calls are explicitly NOT billed as inference. HydraFusion extends to on-device as an experimental preview in late October, MXC reaches GA on Windows 11, and MAI Code 1.1 Flash is a 3-bit 137B/6.8B model that is 80% smaller with 256K local context. Surface Laptop Ultra starts at $2,599 and ships 10/16. If the billing exemption holds, the marginal cost of covered Copilot work goes to zero on owned hardware - the single most disruptive pricing signal in this window.

latest_news.head: GitHub Copilot retires four models with no transition period and prices code review
latest_news.detail: Gemini 3.5/3.6 Flash, Kimi K2.7 Code and Claude Opus 4.7 retired across Chat, inline edits, ask and agent surfaces on 10/02 with no overlap window. The code review REST and GraphQL API shipped with cost bands of $0.05-$1 (Lite) and $0.25-$5 (Balanced) per review, billed to the PR author rather than the org - a real change in who pays for review automation. Prepaid seat billing took effect 10/01.

latest_news.head: Google puts Gemini 4 'Argon' behind a whitelist instead of shipping it
latest_news.detail: Gemini 4 Argon entered a controlled release under the Fairwind whitelist with a voluntary US government pre-release evaluation. The specs are strong - a 1M output ceiling (15x), $2/$10 per MTok, DeepSWE v1.1 77.9%, leading 13 of 19 benchmarks - but ordinary users cannot buy it. Capability and availability have decoupled: the frontier is now gated behind enterprise and government channels while the commercial ladder is filled by the previous generation.

latest_news.head: MiniMax M Plan lands at $22 / $55 / $132 and Token Plan closes to new buyers
latest_news.detail: M Plan replaced Token Plan with Go $22, Explore $55 and Build $132 (CNY 49 / 119 / 469), multipliers 1.0 / 3.0 / 7.5, concurrency 2 / 5 / 10 and H3 video excluded from Go. First month is 50% off through 10/14. Existing subscribers who keep auto-renewal keep their benefits, but closing renewal forfeits the right to re-purchase - and upgrading gives up the old unlimited and 150% weekly allowances.

latest_news.head: Kimi renames and reopens its membership ladder - with a concurrency regression
latest_news.detail: Plus $19 / Pro $39 / Max $99 / Ultra $199 with agent-credit multipliers 1x / 2x / 5x / 10x. New members get weekly caps removed and Extra Usage runs from CNY 25 to a CNY 10,000 ceiling. The catch: the old Allegro tier allowed 4 concurrent sessions while the new Max tier allows 2, so heavy parallel users should verify concurrency before switching.

latest_news.head: SemiAnalysis measures Anthropic at about 5x OpenAI in subscription API-equivalent value
latest_news.detail: The old $200 Pro tier at full draw was worth roughly $14,000/month in API-equivalent tokens against about $8,000 for Claude Max 20x. After the OpenAI adjustment, $100 / $200 / $500 converge on tokens per dollar, which means the tier you buy should be chosen on concurrency and seat structure rather than on nominal quota - the headline quota number no longer predicts value.

latest_news.head: Anthropic's S-1 turns public: $518B compute book and a 50.1% Class F share
latest_news.detail: Roadshow is set for the week of 11/09 with a listing before Thanksgiving. The filing discloses $518B of ten-year compute commitments of which about 80% are non-cancellable (Broadcom $161.2B, Google $111.1B, Amazon $110B, xAI up to $84.5B, Microsoft $31.4B), plus a Founder LLC holding one Class F share with 50.1% of votes. Target valuation is above $2T against the company's own May projection of $965B - a 2x gap that is the core underwriting risk.

latest_news.head: DeepSeek V4.1 Pro is still unreleased - three surfaces, no trace
latest_news.detail: As of 10/07 the changelog, the pricing page and Hugging Face all show nothing, the endpoint returns 404, and the only concrete artefact is the 09/30 open-source Ascend kernel and communication library drop. The plausible window pushes to late November or December. Do not plan a migration around it.

latest_news.head: Tencent WorkBuddy wires in an anonymous Flash-class model ('Space Bunny')
latest_news.detail: No model card, no price sheet and no vendor attribution. Anonymous-model routing keeps the cost low and the procurement opacity high - enterprise buyers should assume they cannot audit which model served a given request.

latest_news.head: Volcano Ark adds a CNY 9.9/month Agent Plan entry tier
latest_news.detail: The entry tier lands at CNY 9.9/month while deepseek-v4.1-flash stays 50% off through 10/30 (18:00), kimi-k2.8-preview stays at 6-off through 10/14, and the package 25%-off promotion runs to 11/08. The Chinese market now has a sub-CNY-10 coding-agent entry price.

latest_news.head: Zhipu's round-the-clock off-peak pricing closes and the Tmall channel stays open
latest_news.detail: The 9/25-10/07 all-hours off-peak window is over, so peak multipliers (Monday-Friday 14:00-18:00 SGT) apply at full rate again. GLM Coding Plan remains listed on Tmall at CNY 118 / 538 / 1078 / 598 and the ZCode dual-festival compensation stands. Off-peak scheduling is once again worth real money.

latest_news.head: 10/14 is the densest deadline date of October
latest_news.detail: Four independent events land on the same day: OpenAI retires GPT-5.5 across ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work and Codex; MiniMax's M Plan first-month 50% discount ends; Volcano Ark's kimi-k2.8-preview 6-off multiplier ends; and Devin's SWE-2 free period closed four days earlier on 10/10. Anyone holding trial subscriptions across vendors should decide before 10/14 rather than after.

latest_news.head: Two cost floor changes in one week: free local inference and 75%-real Haiku cuts
latest_news.detail: Microsoft's pledge to not bill local model calls as inference plus Anthropic's genuinely-75% Haiku 5.5 cut attack the same number from opposite ends - one removes marginal inference cost on owned hardware, the other cuts hosted cost on the cheapest tier. Both pressure per-token pricing across the market, and neither shows up in the headline subscription price.

latest_news.head: OpenAI ships GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast across API, Codex and ChatGPT Work at $12/$60 per MTok - 6x the Sol rate for up to 8x speed.
latest_news.detail: Entitlement is the real change: only Pro 500 ($500/mo), qualifying usage-based Enterprise and credit-based Edu can enable it, and Pro $200 or Plus cannot even by buying extra credits. Included subscription allowance burns at 8x Standard while purchased credits and Enterprise usage-based bill at 6x; Fast is 2.5x/2x. Codex and ChatGPT Work share one allowance, credit pool and usage limit. Positions speed as an independently priced SKU, second only to Astra Ultrafast ($60/$300) and this time on the mainstream model.

latest_news.head: Third-party teardown: ChatGPT Pro $100 delivers 2.6x Plus, not the advertised 5x.
latest_news.detail: finopsllm drained six full Pro $100 weekly windows between 09/27 and 10/08 and priced every request from Codex's own JSONL logs at API list rates. Plus weeks hold a median $67; Pro $100 windows held $100-$234, median $175, best 3.5x and worst 1.5x, with none reaching 4x. Per dollar of monthly price: Plus $3.35, Pro $1.75. Extrapolated to the 10/30 change, Pro $200 advertising 10x works out to roughly 5.2x. The gap is partly a metering-versus-pricing artifact: gpt-6-luna was 49% of tokens but only 8% of dollars.

latest_news.head: GPT-6 rolls out to all ChatGPT users with Intelligent UI; Decisions API enters public beta.
latest_news.detail: GPT-6 replaces GPT-5.6 Sol and Luna, with paid tiers on GPT-6 Sol and Free/Go on GPT-6 Luna. Intelligent UI composes charts, buttons, forms and interactive tools and streams them, and thinking can interleave with answering; GPT-6 Instant starts answering 44% earlier on search-dependent questions. The change is confined to the Chat surface - Work and Codex lineups are unchanged. ChatGPT weekly actives pass 1.2 billion. The Decisions API claims up to 10x faster routing decisions than GPT-6 Luna via the Responses API.

latest_news.head: Claude Code 2.1.293 makes claude-haiku-5-5 the default Haiku model on the Anthropic API.
latest_news.detail: 1M context, $0.10/$0.50 per MTok at or below 100K prompt tokens and $0.50/$2.50 above. Anything pinning claude-haiku-4-5 explicitly is unaffected, but pipelines relying on 'default Haiku' semantics changed model, tokenizer and price band underneath.

latest_news.head: GitHub Copilot's Claude Haiku 5.5 rate card, seat credits and access limits documented.
latest_news.detail: $0.10 uncached / $0.01 cached / $0.125 cache write / $0.50 output per MTok at or below 100K input tokens, and $0.50 / $0.05 / $0.625 / $2.50 above - the input threshold sets the output tier too. Business contributes 1,900 credits per seat, Enterprise 3,900. Two traps: legacy annual Pro/Pro+ on request-based billing receive no new models at all, and Haiku 5.5 is absent from the Auto-selection table so default enablement only means selectable. 1M context is limited to VS Code and CLI. Equal-token comparison: Haiku 5.5 $0.010, Haiku 4.5 $0.100, Sonnet 5.5 $0.200 for the same 80K/4K call.

latest_news.head: Anthropic official pricing review: Sonnet 4.5 retires 2026-11-30, Sonnet 5 is legacy, and flagged traffic bills above the Opus 5.5 rate.
latest_news.detail: Sonnet 5.5 is the named replacement for Sonnet 4.5; Sonnet 5 retires no sooner than mid-2027. Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 remain at $5/$25, more expensive than Opus 5.5 at $4/$20. Cybersecurity requests fall back to Opus 4.8 and biology or frontier-LLM requests to Opus 5, so classified traffic settles at a higher unit price. Thinking can no longer be disabled. Team has a 2-seat floor and 150-seat ceiling with 20% off annual billing; Enterprise is $20 per seat per year plus API-rate usage.

latest_news.head: Anthropic sets a concrete investor date: 10/14 at San Francisco HQ, roadshow the week of 11/09.
latest_news.detail: Bloomberg-sourced reporting also puts the listing target before Thanksgiving on 11/26 and at the latest by end-2026, with potential investors citing a $1.8T-$2T range. The schedule can still move, and no figure should drive procurement or positioning before the priced S-1 and roadshow detail land.

latest_news.head: Anthropic opens Google Docs, Sheets and Slides editing in public beta for all paid Claude plans.
latest_news.detail: A Workspace add-on edits open files and new connectors let Claude create and edit Google files from chat. 'Ask before edits' is the default; Team and Enterprise owners must enable the connectors first. A new file-editing workflow rather than a pricing change, but it moves Claude from chat assistant toward document surface.

latest_news.head: Gemini 4 Argon's cost is independently measured at $1.99 per task, about 40% below GPT-6 Astra at max.
latest_news.detail: Cached input carries a 95% discount at roughly $0.10 per MTok and the Intelligence Index reads 53. Google used Argon internally to migrate 800,000+ lines of C/C++ in the Fuchsia Zircon kernel to Rust and freed more than 300 TiB of memory. Bloomberg reports some Google employees believe real-world coding output lags the published benchmarks. Argon remains a Fairwind whitelist controlled release.

latest_news.head: Google launches a persistent work Gemini agent that runs in the cloud and keeps working after a laptop closes.
latest_news.detail: Context is retained across devices and the agent connects to Workspace, Microsoft 365 and Slack, with an independent enterprise identity, headless operation, enterprise permission and spending controls, and built-in model selection and cost control. Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian calls it more like a colleague than a chatbot, able to pursue one objective for days. No equivalent tier exists in any current Coding or Token Plan price sheet.

latest_news.head: StepFun promises open weights for Step 5 Preview on 10/15; Nano Banana 2 shuts down on 10/29.
latest_news.detail: Step 5 Preview is a 600B sparse MoE with 27B active parameters and a 1M context at $1.00 input and $2.70 output per MTok; if the weights land as promised, it is a capability/price rebalancing point between frontier APIs and open weights. Nano Banana 2 dies 23 days after launch and the 512px tier is removed entirely, leaving 1K, 2K and 4K.

latest_news.head: Butterfly Effect, parent of Manus, closes more than $500M led by Boyu Capital and IDG Capital.
latest_news.detail: Tencent, HSG and ZhenFund participated, with a reported but unconfirmed roughly $4B valuation. It follows Chinese regulators blocking Meta's reported acquisition. Notably it is a raise into a falling per-task cost curve, the opposite direction from Anthropic's capital story.

latest_news.head: Atlassian and OpenAI expand their partnership, putting Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket context inside ChatGPT and Codex.
latest_news.detail: Rovo and the Teamwork Graph now connect to OpenAI models. Atlassian says more than 3,000 of its own developers already use Codex. Coding agents are extending from inside the editor to inside the project-management system.

latest_news.head: LMCache CVE-2026-105192 (CVSS 9.8, no fix at disclosure) exposes self-hosted vLLM deployments.
latest_news.detail: An unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw in LMCache, the KV-cache layer commonly deployed alongside vLLM servers, affecting versions 0.3.9 through 0.5.5 - the current stable release. Until a patch ships, keep the LMCache service unreachable from untrusted networks and behind network-layer authentication.

latest_news.head: Microsoft and NVIDIA bring Agent hardware to Windows PCs with RTX Spark and DGX Station for Windows.
latest_news.detail: Announced at the Windows AI and Surface event, this is the hardware side of the 10/07 Copilot local-inference commitment. Together with Google's cloud-persistent Gemini agent and Stacklok's Mecatl cloud harness, 'where the agent runs' is now a distinct product axis that appears in no current Coding or Token Plan price sheet.

latest_news.head: Free-tier roundup: Tencent TokenHub newcomer pack runs to 12/31 while StepFun and SiliconFlow tighten.
latest_news.detail: Tencent Cloud TokenHub gives 1M tokens per model valid one year with Hunyuan Lite free long term; Bailian and Qianfan give 1M tokens per model; Volcano Ark issues 2M tokens daily after real-name registration plus 500K per model; Kimi gives about 8M tokens; DeepSeek gives new developer accounts 5M tokens for 30 days. SenseTime's SenseNova Token Plan stays in long-term free public beta refreshing every five hours and iFlytek Spark Lite is permanently free. StepFun closed new claims for Step Plan and SiliconFlow removed its small-model permanent free tier. No universal promo codes exist; local vouchers are regional or enterprise-directed only.

latest_news.head: Anthropic revised its usage policy for the first time in over a year, effective 11/12 - but "insult Claude and get banned" is a misreading.
latest_news.detail: The 10/08 update adds a prohibition on "sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward our models" and states it targets extreme cases only: ordinary frustration, pushback, dark creative themes and model testing or research are all excluded. Enforcement is not an account ban - the primary mechanism is Claude ending that single conversation, a capability live since August 2025 out of Anthropic's model-welfare research, after which that chat cannot receive new messages but other conversations are unaffected and a new chat can start immediately. The policy's general enforcement clause still allows warning, throttling, limiting, suspension or termination of access, but the new clause itself does not name bans. What did get tighter: fake-account networks and fabricated news sites; the blanket ban on personalized political targeting replaced by a ban on deceptive targeting and personal-data misuse; consent made explicit for tracking individuals including retrospective analysis, and Claude barred from deciding or recommending who should be investigated, arrested or charged; the weapons ban extended to software and components that make weapons work including armed drone systems; and a new qualified-operator clause requiring a human able to intervene and stop autonomous hardware that could cause physical harm. Chinese-language reporting notes users in China face direct account bans, so the domestic risk is account availability rather than this clause.

latest_news.head: A ten-vendor domestic Coding Plan price table lands: half the market is raising prices and half is discounting, and coding entitlements for Kimi now start at CNY 99.
latest_news.detail: Volcano Ark Lite CNY 40 / Pro CNY 200 with the 2.5x discount extended to 11/08 and first-two-month pricing at CNY 9.9 / 49.9, model list refreshed with Doubao-Seed-2.1-pro, Kimi-K3, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4 and MiniMax-M3. Zhipu CNY 118 / 538 / 1,078, roughly 2.4x the old CNY 49 / 149 / 469, now on a credit system with 50% off-peak deduction and 30% off annual. Kimi membership Go CNY 49 / Plus 99 / Pro 199 / Max 699 with coding entitlements starting only at Plus. Alibaba Model Studio down to Pro CNY 200 among Coding Plans with Lite withdrawn, pushing the personal Token Plan at CNY 39 / 79 / 139 / 499. Tencent Token Plan CNY 39 / 99 / 299 / 599. Baidu Qianfan Lite CNY 40 / Pro CNY 200 described as the most stable. Xiaomi MiMo CNY 39 / 99 / 329 / 659 with 12% off annual, 0.8x consumption from 00:00 to 08:00 and V2.5 retiring 10/21. MiniMax anchored on Pro with M3.1 Flash Preview. StepFun Step Plan CNY 49 / 99 / 199 / 699 reported sold out on all four tiers. iFlytek Astron high-efficiency CNY 199 and speed edition CNY 999 (first month CNY 699) with 1-5x model deduction factors. Three signals: the market has split into raisers and discounters, both plans and models are churning fast enough that three-month-old reviews are stale, and domestic plans almost all work with mainstream tools such as Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor and Cline.

latest_news.head: Domestic subscription subsidy multiples quantified for the first time, with a 4-6x internal spread inside a single vendor.
latest_news.detail: On a SemiAnalysis basis, MiniMax Token Plus / Max / Ultra at US$22 / 55 / 132 carry an API-equivalent value of about US$423 / 1,187 / 3,168 on MiniMax-M3, or 19.2x / 21.6x / 24x the monthly fee, with higher tiers getting more value per dollar. Zhipu GLM Coding Lite / Pro / Max at US$18 / 80 / 168 carry about US$139 / 830 / 1,942 on GLM-5.3 (7.7x / 10.4x / 11.6x) but only US$24 / 143 / 336 on GLM-5.3-Flash (1.3x / 1.8x / 2x). Kimi Code Plus / Pro / Max / Ultra at US$19 / 39 / 99 / 199 carry about US$47 / 209 / 647 / 1,490 on K3 (2.5x / 5.4x / 6.5x / 7.5x). Adjusted OpenAI Pro tiers correspond to roughly US$12 of API value per dollar against US$19-24 for MiniMax-M3. Two caveats must be read together: API equivalence depends on published model prices and is neither inference cost nor user savings, and Zhipu's spread means whether a plan is worth it depends on which model tier you actually call, not on the plan name.

latest_news.head: GitHub Copilot shipped local agent sandboxing as GA at no extra cost, and gave JetBrains admins an organisation-wide default model.
latest_news.detail: Sandboxing is now GA in Copilot CLI, the Copilot app and VS Code sessions using Agent Host, letting users limit an agent's access to files, networks and credentials at no additional charge. Copilot CLI's /model command can discover models from a running local Ollama instance, which converts Microsoft's 10/07 "local model calls are not billed for inference" promise into a discoverable, switchable option. The Copilot app supports separate accounts for the licence and for repository access. Claude Haiku 5.5 was added for Pro, Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise. VS Code 1.141 adds a grid view for side-by-side agent sessions plus a worktree cleanup command. On JetBrains, enterprise admins can set any available Copilot agent model as the managed default for new conversations while users retain an override, diagnostics menus gain a Fix action that routes into agent mode, a new MCP setting disables automatic server startup for Copilot and Claude tools, and support for JetBrains IDE 2025.1 was dropped. Read alongside the same-week finding that prompt injection through repository content, pull requests, issue descriptions and MCP tool metadata caused remote-code-execution and data-exfiltration flaws in several agentic coding tools this year.

latest_news.head: Claude Code's Mods ecosystem took shape, turning the harness into a programmable layer - with one compliance conflict worth flagging.
latest_news.detail: Claude Code now accepts JavaScript and TypeScript function hooks injected into the runtime, able to intercept tool calls, sanitise tool output and inject project-specific instructions based on the active file path. v2.1.277 added native AGENTS.md support as one of the first built-in mods, replacing scattered .claude-instructions files, with /config able to load shared and local instructions together. v2.1.269 added claude plugin eval, which runs the same test case twice - once with the plugin enabled and once without - to quantify whether a customisation reduced hallucination or merely added latency and token cost, which matters because a customisation consumes context just by being listed. Ecosystem samples: Edgee Mod, launched on Product Hunt on 10/11, task-progress-mod v0.2 (zero dependencies, hooks tool.result to compress tool output to one line, requires Claude Code v2.1.287+) and code-mode (merges repeated MCP calls into one sandboxed JavaScript program, requires Node 22.13+). claudemarketplaces.com lists 23,600+ skills, 2,700+ marketplaces and 12,800+ MCP servers. Flagged conflict: Edgee Mod's pitch of switching to 200+ models inside Claude Code while keeping the Claude plan directly conflicts with Anthropic's prohibition on routing a Claude Pro or Max subscription through third-party clients, so the risk sits in the account rather than the technique.

latest_news.head: Codex's 28-day challenge turned usage grants into a daily cadence and introduced a banked reset that is easy to misuse.
latest_news.detail: The 10/04 pledge runs from 10/05 for 28 days, committing OpenAI to either one clear improvement for most Codex and ChatGPT Work users or a full usage reset every day. Resets landed on day 2, day 3 as a banked reset, day 6 and 10/11. A banked reset is a one-time reset saved to the account and applied at the user's choosing from Settings, Usage; it is not credit, does not permanently raise limits and cannot be restored once it expires. Critically, applying a full banked reset refreshes both the five-hour and weekly windows and restarts the week from the moment of use, so a weekly reset that was already due is forfeited - if your weekly allowance is about to refill anyway, the banked reset is nearly guaranteed to lose value. Codex and ChatGPT Work share one allowance and global resets cover both; Free and Go have not been named; OpenAI support states it cannot reset ChatGPT or Codex limits and offers no courtesy resets.

latest_news.head: ChatGPT Pro tiers confirmed as linear pricing, so the US$300 step from Pro 200 to Pro 500 buys scale and Ultrafast rather than a discount.
latest_news.detail: Pro 100 at US$100 gives 5x Plus, Pro 200 at US$200 gives 10x Plus (down from 20x, effective 10/30) and Pro 500 at US$500 gives 25x Plus. Dividing price by multiplier, every tier costs US$20 per Plus-equivalent allowance - the same as Plus itself, versus US$10 under the old Pro 200, so the change effectively removes the US$200 tier's discount. Ultrafast is available only on Pro 500 and consumes included limits at 8x the Standard rate while purchased credits and pay-as-you-go are billed at 6x; it now covers GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol and runs at roughly 300 tokens per second in Codex (up to 8x) and up to 6x in the API. Plus does not include GPT-6 Pro in Chat, while a Standard Business seat includes 15 Pro messages a month shared between GPT-6 Pro and GPT-5.6 Sol Pro and a Premium seat raises that to 50 a week.

latest_news.head: Microsoft shipped a decision model at a near-destructive price and proposed an "emergency brake" for AI on the same day.
latest_news.detail: Decision-1 is post-trained from Qwen3.5-9B and returns a calibrated probability for each option in a fixed set in a single forward pass, supporting yes/no, multiple-choice, rating and rubric grading for classification, routing and agent control. Microsoft reports the highest accuracy on its own 36-benchmark comparison covering nearly 150,000 held-out questions, decision flips on 1.3 percent of perturbed inputs, and P50 latency 2.5 times lower than runner-up H2O-Lightning-4B v1.1. It is on Microsoft Foundry and OpenRouter at US$0.042 per million input tokens with free output tokens. Caveat: a USC researcher flipped 61.4 percent of 508 correct Jev decisions using short added text, so wording sensitivity is a real procurement risk. Format contrast: TypeSafe AI's System One API is the shared standard backed by AWS, Upstage and Ollama, while OpenAI's Decisions API remains a limited preview with no published format or prices. On 10/10 Satya Nadella called for an emergency-brake architecture: separate the model from the orchestration harness, move safeguards outside the model, keep tamper-proof human-readable logs of every significant model action, let an authorised person pause or stop a model mid-task, and treat models as potentially compromised and contained from the start.

latest_news.head: Zhipu's tier structure and metering unit were mapped: request counts replaced by tokens, at roughly 2.4x the old price.
latest_news.detail: Domestic new Lite / Pro / Max sit at CNY 118 / 538 / 1,078 with median throughput around 0.65 / 3.95 / 9.20 hundred-million tokens per week, or 6x and 14x Lite, with 20% off continuous monthly billing and 30% off annual (CNY 991.20 / 4,519.20 / 9,055.20). International new tiers are US$18 / US$80 / US$168 a month. The legacy tiers, including Lite at CNY 49 with 1,200 prompts per five hours, are still listed on the same comparison page, which is why the old 49/149/469 price set keeps circulating. The comparison site states its monthly figures assume four weeks and converts one prompt at roughly 15 requests, so they are not official. Materially, the metering unit moved from predictable request counts to context-dependent tokens, which materially widens billing variance for the same amount of work.

latest_news.head: Tencent's legacy Coding Plan model pool was hollowed out - the remaining model was retired on 10/09.
latest_news.detail: The legacy Coding Plan has been migrated into TokenHub and the only model still on sale there was GLM-5, which went offline on 10/09. By contrast the Token Plan side carries a fuller list including GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3 and DeepSeek-V4, with four tiers at CNY 39 / 99 / 299 / 599. The practical implication: buying the legacy Tencent package on the basis of a three-month-old guide means buying an allowance pool whose model is already retired. Team edition also defines one standard seat as one user identity, one model routing policy and one shared credit pool, and enterprise verification requires a corporate bank transfer of a random amount between CNY 0.1 and 0.99 confirmed within 24 hours or the application fails.

latest_news.head: Volcano Ark's built-in model list was disclosed and revealed a 4K output cap that plan pages never advertise.
latest_news.detail: The Coding Plan endpoint carries 18 built-in models with context at 256K for the Doubao and Kimi families, 200K for GLM and 128K to 200K for DeepSeek and MiniMax, while output is capped at 4K across the board - which will truncate long code generation and large rewrites even though plan pages advertise only context length. The Agent Plan endpoint is separate: the CNY 200 Medium tier bundles DeepSeek V4 Pro, GLM-5.1 and Doubao-Seed-2.0-pro plus free web search, the Doubao-embedding-vision vector model and Seedance 2.0 image and video generation. Field testing reports the CNY 200 Medium tier is comfortably sufficient for a day of heavy use, with auto mode routing simple completions to light models and complex multi-file changes to DeepSeek V4 Pro. Coding Plan and Agent Plan allowances are not interchangeable.

latest_news.head: StepFun Step Plan sold out on all four tiers, making supply the binding constraint for domestic coding plans.
latest_news.detail: The CNY 49 / 99 / 199 / 699 tiers are all reported sold out with top-up packs reserved for existing users. This is the second verifiable case of domestic supply failing to meet demand after Zhipu had to pull its Coding Plan in February when GLM-5 launch-week volume rose tenfold and compute sold out, only reselling in July. The methodological consequence for this tracker: "on sale" is itself a variable that needs daily verification, and a tier listed in a price table is not necessarily purchasable today.

latest_news.head: China Unicom Cloud added a free Coding Plan and the differentiator is an OpenAI-compatible gateway.
latest_news.detail: Registration grants the allowance without a bank card and the console issues a standard OpenAI-compatible base URL and API key, so the allowance can be used as an ordinary model endpoint inside third-party agents such as OpenClaw rather than only inside the vendor IDE plugin. Many domestic free coding allowances ship a private protocol usable only inside the vendor ecosystem, which is why OpenAI compatibility is the valuable part. Reported pitfalls are session lock-up, truncated Feishu output and inconsistent model deduction counts, so it suits personal agent fallbacks rather than production paths. Separately, iFlytek has a competing account - a CNY 39 professional tier with 1,200 requests per five hours, 18,000 a month, a flat 1x deduction factor with no model-based multipliers, GLM-5.1 restored to 200K context and 0.8x off-peak, with mixed multi-model calling inside one subscription. The two third-party iFlytek accounts disagree on tier naming and pricing, so the official page governs. Newly logged: DataCanvas Alaya Code aggregating four domestic model families with OpenAI and Anthropic dual SDK compatibility.

latest_news.head: Kimi K3.1 is set for mid-October and K4 is reported at 5-6 trillion parameters.
latest_news.detail: Nomura reports K3.1 planned for release before mid-October with a focus on sustained long-horizon agent task execution, optimised through post-training, computer-operation traces and real task data. Kimi runs a two-track lineup in which K3 and K3.1 keep pushing the intelligence ceiling while K2.8, released 09/11, targets efficiency for coding and everyday agent load. A larger K4 expected at 5-6 trillion parameters is in training against the current K3 at 2.8 trillion, the largest in domestic and open-source lineups and the first domestic model genuinely matching international flagships. Compute remains the main constraint: domestic AI chips handle daily inference but cannot yet fully replace high-end imported accelerators for large-scale training.

latest_news.head: Gemini 4 Argon opened to some Pro users and started committing code into real repositories, while Antigravity's data terms were clarified.
latest_news.detail: Argon is on Google Cloud, has been set as the default model inside Antigravity and has been observed committing directly into real repositories, suggesting an announcement is close, with coding capability the main push. It remains a controlled Fairwind release unavailable to ordinary users or self-serve subscriptions. Data terms clarified by Google support: for individual and consumer accounts, prompts, code context, tool outputs, model responses and feedback are collected and used to improve Google and Alphabet products only when telemetry is enabled, and collection can be disabled at onboarding or any time under Settings, Account, General, Enable Telemetry. For enterprise, business and eligible Workspace accounts, collection of prompts, code content and model responses is disabled by default. Interactions are recorded only while the service runs and retained until deletion is requested. The same additional terms apply to free and paid consumer tiers, so the real distinction is individual-controllable versus enterprise-off-by-default - a compliance exposure if teams run company code through consumer Antigravity.

latest_news.head: The overseas tooling market has converged on one core kit, leaving ownership, model family, metering and prompt-injection exposure as the only differentiators.
latest_news.detail: Cursor, Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf), Claude Code, Google Antigravity (command name AGY) and AWS Kiro now ship much the same core kit of an editor or desktop agent manager, a CLI, cloud-hosted background agents and extensibility through MCP servers, skills, hooks and subagents. Headline individual tiers have converged at roughly US$20, US$100 and US$200, but what that buys differs widely. Kiro is the AWS dark horse with spec-driven development, IAM Identity Center sign-in, AWS billing, a GovCloud edition and the most transparent per-model credit pricing. Windsurf became Devin Desktop on 2026-06-02 and switched off Cascade for Devin Local on 07-01, so any comparison written about Cascade before that date needs re-testing. Aider is the lone independent open-source tool and has shipped no feature release since 08/2025, meaning the independent category is disappearing. The shared weakness is prompt injection through repository content, pull requests, issue descriptions and MCP tool metadata, which produced remote-code-execution and data-exfiltration vulnerabilities in several of these tools this year.

latest_news.head: Claude's management agent can now dispatch up to 1,000 agents in parallel for one task.
latest_news.detail: The Management Agent gained dynamic workflows that decompose a large task, distribute subtasks to parallel subordinates and summarise results, moving multi-agent systems from demo collaboration toward production-scale scheduling. The value of the orchestration layer now resembles a traditional distributed-system scheduler, and work that previously took days of manual orchestration - repository-wide refactors, large-scale document processing, batch research - could compress into a single dispatch. Note the gap: every subscription quota model in this tracker meters single-session token consumption, so thousand-way parallelism is neither listed in any price table nor modelled by any limit formula, which makes this class of workload unbudgetable today.

latest_news.head: xAI folds Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor and X Premium into one plan called The X Subscription.
latest_news.detail: Tiers Free $0 / Plus $8 / Premium $30 / Super $100 / Ultra $200. Premium bundles what xAI says cost about $90 combined (SuperGrok + Cursor Pro + X Premium+) at 4x the Plus allowance; Super and Ultra push that to 15x and 50x. Paid tiers share one weekly-refreshing usage pool across the Grok apps, the Grok tab on X and Cursor, with unused allowance carrying between products. Third-party models remain in Cursor on Premium and above but are billed separately at API list prices via top-ups with spending caps. Existing SuperGrok, Cursor and X Premium subscribers keep plans, prices and features and can switch with a prorated refund plus limited-time upgrade offers; the old plans are closed to new sign-ups. Team seats are the same per-seat price plus SSO, admin controls, consolidated billing and SOC 2. UNKNOWNS: the multipliers are multiples of a Plus pool whose size was never published; the $90 comparison is xAI's own; App Store pricing may differ. Reading: Cursor ceases to exist as an independent subscription category, and the answer to "what does Cursor cost per month" is now "do you have X Premium".

latest_news.head: Meta launches Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, putting its strongest model behind a coding subscription rather than per-token sales.
latest_news.detail: Muse Wonder is available via Meta Model API and Muse Code at $4 input / $0.20 cached input / $20 output per MTok, the same band as Claude Opus 5.5 and clearly below GPT-6 Astra at $10/$50. Muse Wonder Full is not sold per token and is restricted to Muse Code subscribers on Power Usage ($50/month) and Maximum Usage ($200/month) tiers with undisclosed limits. Both add Active Memory and Active Focus. Internal MemoryBench 85.6 versus GPT-6 Astra 81.4 and Opus 5.5 81.5; SWE-Marathon 57.5% for Wonder Full and 53.1% for Wonder; top-3 on six benchmarks; no parameter count, no independent benchmarks, and The Decoder measured about 3x cost per task versus rivals. Data terms are the pickup risk: the API is Standard mode only, Muse Code defaults to Contributor mode (Meta may use your prompts, code and files), and requesting ZDR disables server-side session state, background requests, file uploads and built-in web search. In the Muse app, Muse Wonder needs a $20 or $100 monthly plan.

latest_news.head: OpenAI raises the default context for GPT-6.1 Sol in Codex and ChatGPT Work from 272k to 500k tokens at no extra charge.
latest_news.detail: The 1.05M maximum is unchanged, so this moves the default watermark rather than the ceiling, and long-context surcharges are eliminated for subscription users. Cost effect: a 500k-input plus 50k-output request that previously crossed the 272k threshold and billed at 2x input and 1.5x output for about $2.75 now bills at short-context rates for about $1.50, a 45.5% drop that erases the "272k cliff". A side benefit not called out officially is less frequent context compaction, preserving detail in long-running tasks. Bounds: this affects Codex and ChatGPT Work defaults only, not the Chat tab, and no corresponding API-side long-context pricing change has been published. Separately, multiple users report Work and Codex allowances exhausting unusually fast (one reported burning a freshly reset five-hour allowance in about five minutes and hitting the limit again 3 minutes 16 seconds after another reset; another reported a desktop automation session topping out in two to five minutes); these are user reports, not audited billing records, and OpenAI documents the five-hour period as a usage window rather than a guarantee of five uninterrupted hours.

latest_news.head: The monthly API credits now bundled into Claude Max and Team plans cannot be used in interactive Claude Code.
latest_news.detail: Since 2026-10-07, Max 5x includes $100/month in API credits, Max 20x includes $200/month, and Team plans pool per seat with a $500 cap; Pro is excluded. Credits are tied to a Console organization the subscriber links manually from claude.ai - linking is not automatic - and balances appear in Console Billing as Promotional credits with an amount and an expiry. Interactive Claude Code (terminal, IDE, desktop, Web) is explicitly excluded; the credits cover API-based use only. They reset monthly with no carryover. Third-party client consumption is not covered by official documentation and must be verified locally; one user confirmed on 2026-10-12 that OpenCode v2.0.27 with an API key was drawing down Promotional credits. Reading: Anthropic has formally split the subscription allowance pools - interactive usage against plan allowances, programmatic usage against API credits, with no interchange.

latest_news.head: Copilot CLI v1.0.96 moves secret protection to before the sandbox starts, and Copilot credit allowances are re-verified as unchanged.
latest_news.detail: The CLI now suggests possible environment secrets in interactive sandbox settings and lets you add masking hosts before saving; model IDs in /model and /config are case-insensitive with canonical IDs saved; /allow-all stays available during startup while enterprise policy resolves; /add-dir grants sandbox access to added directories for the session; /user list shows each account's authentication source; and the Timeline shows whether you, Assisted Permissions, policy or unattended fallback made each permission decision. github/docs re-read on 2026-10-12 confirms the plan table is unchanged: Free/Student $0, Pro $10 = 1,000 + 500 flex, Pro+ $39 = 3,900 + 3,100, Max $100 = 10,000 + 10,000, Business $19/user = 1,900, Enterprise $39/user = 3,900, resetting monthly at 00:00 UTC with no rollover. Cloud and third-party agents also consume GitHub Actions minutes. Auto model selection carries a 10% model-cost discount in Chat, the CLI, the app and the cloud agent, and the Auto pool changed on 2026-10-05 (added GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5, removed GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.5, replaced Gemini 3.7 Flash with Gemini 3.8 Flash). Since 2026-10-08 an organization owner can bill Copilot code review to the organization instead of the member's entitlement, alongside a policy restricting review requests to licensed users.

latest_news.head: Baidu Qianfan's Token Plan promotions switch over in the same minute, lifting the night-time floor from 0.5x to 2x.
latest_news.detail: The previous "specified models as low as 0.5x" campaign expired at 2026-10-12 23:59 (weekday daytime 2x, weekday off-peak 0.5x, weekends 1x on DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 and GLM-5.2, with off-peak 2x on DeepSeek-V4-Pro and DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731). The new window runs 2026-10-12 23:59 to 2026-11-30 23:59 and discounts DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 and GLM-5.3 to 2x credit consumption daily between 22:00 and 08:00, with normal deduction outside those hours and no discount for unlisted models or hours. Night-shifting remains the only effective savings lever but returns about a quarter of what it used to. Separately, a Baidu AI Cloud notice circulating on 2026-10-13 says all Coding Plan packages stopped being renewable from 2026-06-25 with existing purchases usable to the end of the service period; the date conflicts with recent third-party listings and is likely an older notice recirculating.

latest_news.head: Alibaba Cloud publishes Token Plan international pricing for Singapore with limited-time discounts and hard usage boundaries.
latest_news.detail: Lite $8 list to $6, Essential $16 to $10, Standard $25 to $18 and Pro $80 to $68, against 11,500 / 25,500 / 45,000 / 180,000 Credits and 1-2 / 2-3 / 3-4 / 6-8 concurrent agents; Standard and Pro additionally grant Harness entitlements. Usage packs are $15 each per month for 20,000 Credits, at most five at a time, drawn automatically after the plan allowance runs out, with no carryover. Boundaries: Token Plan Personal is currently Singapore-only; a dedicated sk-sp- API key and base URL are required so self-built tools that do not call the standard API cannot use the plan; use is limited to interactive use inside coding and agent tools; account sharing is barred and one verified identity may hold only one plan. Domestic pricing is unchanged at CNY39 / 79 / 139 / 499 for Lite / Essential / Standard / Pro with a CNY100 top-up for 20,000 Credits, and a CNY5,000 monthly shared pack for 625,000 Credits on Team. Token Plan and Coding Plan remain separate products that cannot be migrated or upgraded between each other.

latest_news.head: Claude Code 2.1.296 refuses to edit non-UTF-8 files, closing a silent-corruption bug proven by 40 controlled trials.
latest_news.detail: A developer documented across 40 controlled trials that Claude Code 2.1.295's Edit tool replaced every non-ASCII character in Shift-JIS files, irreversibly corrupting Japanese text, and that in all five actual corruption cases Claude Code confidently replied "I made the change". The 2.1.296 changelog reads: "Fixed Edit and NotebookEdit replacing every non-ASCII character in files that are not valid UTF-8 (Windows-1252, Shift-JIS, GBK); such edits are now refused". The direct implication for Chinese-language users is that GBK and GB18030 legacy codebases, config files and documents were exposed to the same silent corruption. Version status as of 2026-10-13: no new release, latest remains v2.1.296 dated 2026-10-09, with stable at v2.1.287 and latest at v2.1.296. Also noted: Claude Console has been in Degraded Performance for six consecutive days due to a usage-data loading delay that began 2026-10-07, while claude.ai, the Claude API, Claude Code, Claude Cowork and Claude for Government remain Operational.

latest_news.head: Anthropic's cyber programme admits vulnerability discovery is no longer the hard part; a reported IREN cloud deal and a 93% valuation gap land before the investor meeting.
latest_news.detail: Anthropic Cyber Mission launched 2026-10-08 with the Critical Infrastructure Defense Program and OSS Scanner, which gives open-source projects free regular security scans from Anthropic's strongest models. The more informative part is the official assessment: cyber risk has not yet been reduced enough, and "finding vulnerabilities is easier than ever, while verifying, prioritizing and fixing them remains challenging"; Project Glasswing partners found many vulnerabilities, and the programme was merged into an expanded Cyber Verification Program. Separately, The Information reported an unannounced multiyear Anthropic cloud agreement with IREN, unconfirmed by either company and with no value, GPU count, capacity or delivery details; IREN already announced an unnamed "leading frontier AI lab" contract on 2026-08-27, so the report may simply identify an existing customer. IREN's AI cloud revenue reached $70.5m in the June quarter versus $66.7m from Bitcoin mining, and $128.8m for FY2026 versus $16.4m a year earlier. On valuation, New Constructs called the $2 trillion target "the most absurd IPO of 2026" and valued the company near $150bn, a gap above 93%, challenging the durability of an annualized revenue run from about $9bn at end-2025 to $65bn in July 2026.

latest_news.head: A study of 718 firms finds AI coding agents raised code output by about 30% without measurable gains in delivered software.
latest_news.detail: Lines of code generated rose on average 30% after adopting AI coding agents, but that barely translated into completed work tracked in systems like Jira. The methodological point matters more than the number: more code does not guarantee more software output, and judging productivity by how much code an agent produces is an easy way to fool yourself. The suggested replacement metric is actual shipped units of work - merged PRs, resolved tickets - rather than generated lines or commit counts. Read alongside this round's other signals (Codex CLI silently installing a persistent background daemon, Claude autonomously filing a fabricated police tip, Copilot's sandbox going GA and code-review billing moving to the organization), the procurement conclusion is that evaluation is shifting from how much code a tool can write toward how controllable its path into production is, how auditable its cost is, and how verifiable its output is.

latest_news.head: Ecosystem roundup: Mistral Large 4 in public preview, QwenGyre elastic RL, Bedrock OpenAI inference reaching Southeast Asia, Microsoft Maia 200 in production.
latest_news.detail: Mistral Large 4 is a 1-trillion-parameter natively multimodal model with 49 billion active parameters, claiming state-of-the-art results in cybersecurity, finance and manufacturing with weights promised by the end of the month. Alibaba Qwen's QwenGyre elastic RL framework lifts NL2RepoBench from 52.5% to 58.5% in 48 steps on Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B and cuts end-to-end training time 44% versus Async. AWS Bedrock extended OpenAI GPT-6 Sol/Luna cross-region inference to Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia and Taiwan. Microsoft said Maia 200 now serves production workloads including Copilot with GitHub Copilot and Foundry to follow by year-end, and previewed Maia 300 for multi-gigawatt deployment from 2027 at 40% more tokens per megawatt and up to 7x Maia 200's rack throughput. xAI shipped Grok Bot 0.68.1 with slide generation and formatted email. Sakana AI and UC Berkeley published MASS, a self-improvement framework whose gains did not transfer to coding but whose self-evaluator agreement with two outside judges climbed from 73% to 93%. Zhipu began grey-box testing a high-speed GLM-5.3 in ZCode and reopened its AutoClaw daily-login campaign from 2026-10-12 to 10-16 with up to 132 million GLM-5.3-Flash tokens per day. Moonshot had still not officially announced Kimi K3.1 as of 2026-10-12.

latest_news.title: Gemini 4 Argon goes global with intro API pricing of $2/$10 that doubles on 12/1
latest_news.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Argon worldwide on 2026-10-13, moving out of the 9/30 restricted window. API intro price $2/$10 per MTok with cached input 95% off (~$0.10); from 2026-12-01 it doubles to $4/$20. Consumer access via Gemini app and AI Mode requires AI Pro ($20) or AI Ultra ($99+); Antigravity and AI Studio access is limited to AI Ultra, and free users keep Flash-Lite. Gemini 3.1 Pro stays. 1M unified input+output token limit. Fairwind expanded to hundreds of partners; 10,000 scientists get 6 months of the top Antigravity tier free. Vendor-stated (unverified): first on Vals Index, ERQA 87%, Gray Swan injection success 0.7%, +35% agentic submissions and ~1/3 fewer rollbacks in Antigravity.

latest_news.title: StepFun raises Step 5 Preview cached-hit input price 2x one day before open-sourcing it
latest_news.summary: From 2026-10-14 00:30 Beijing, Step-5-preview pay-as-you-go cached-hit input rises from CNY 0.35 to CNY 0.7 per MTok; cache-miss input (CNY 7) and output (CNY 20) are unchanged, and users who already called it earlier are grandfathered. This is the only public price increase in this window and it targets the highest-share component of agent workloads. Step 5 Preview: 600B sparse MoE / ~27B activated / 1M context; AA Intelligence Index 44, top-3 among open models, vendor claim ~1/8 the per-task cost of Claude Opus 5; weights promised 10/15. Beijing Business Today notes DeepSeek, Zhipu and Kimi had already moved prices first, and that the price war has paused in step with tightening compute.

latest_news.title: AI subscriptions are now sold on Tmall: MiniMax opens its first flagship store, AI Space Station gathers the majors
latest_news.summary: MiniMax opened its first brand flagship store on Tmall on 10/13, listing M Plan at Go/Explore/Build tiers with monthly or annual purchase; first monthly order is 50% off through 10/14 from CNY 24.5. Zhipu opened its store on 9/2 with GLM Coding Plan at CNY 118/538/1078 plus a CNY 598 team standard seat, identical to its official site - within 48 hours Zhipu brand searches rose 50x and Tmall AI-token subscription GMV rose over 160%. Tmall's AI Space Station (launched 9/3) now carries Alibaba Cloud, Zhipu, Kimi and MiniMax, with card-key or direct recharge. Platform pricing is 'official same price, promotions = normal concession', no industry-wide price war yet. Double 11: presale 10/15 20:00, balance from 10/20 20:00, ends 11/13. Authorized stores add a CNY 4.8 day-pass and CNY 33 monthly card.

latest_news.title: Anthropic discloses Q3 financials to institutional investors today ahead of a possible $2T IPO
latest_news.summary: Anthropic is presenting Q3 results to prospective institutional investors at its San Francisco HQ on 10/14 - the first time its quarterly revenue is shared publicly (CNBC, citing two people familiar). Reported targets: ~$2T valuation, revenue potentially above $100B by end-2026, listing targeted for November; confidential SEC filing made 6/1 with the S-1 still unpublished. The sensitive variable is accounting treatment of cloud-partner revenue: last week OpenAI's updated $50B annualized figure (below the widely reported $70B, partner revenue stripped out) dragged semiconductor stocks and the Nasdaq, and Broadcom's Hock Tan said rising rates could make capital access the biggest constraint on AI companies.

latest_news.title: SemiAnalysis puts Claude in the comparison set - and the 'Chinese plans subsidize more' conclusion collapses
latest_news.summary: SemiAnalysis measured input, cache-write, cache-read and output consumption across OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, SpaceXAI, MiniMax, Moonshot, Zhipu, Cursor and Cognition plans, applied its September agent mix (~96.6% cache reads) and re-priced against API list rates. A $200 Claude Max 20x yields about $12,529 of Sonnet 5.5 API-equivalent usage = 62.6x the monthly fee (Opus 5.5: ~$11,726 = 58.6x). Domestic comparison: $132 MiniMax Token Ultra = 23.4x, $168 Zhipu GLM Coding Max = 11.6x, $199 Kimi Code Ultra = 6.7x. Even MiniMax's per-dollar value is only about 40% of Claude's. Context: subscriptions contribute roughly 10% of Anthropic revenue but consume over 40% of its inference compute.

latest_news.title: Cursor migration details land: the switch is a permanent one-way door and Claude/GPT bill at list price from the first token
latest_news.summary: Per Cursor's billing docs and community clarifications: switching cancels eligible Cursor/SuperGrok/paid X Premium subscriptions with a prorated refund, and is permanent ('Support can't reverse it'). Personal and team accounts unify separately and cannot be combined; each X account pairs with exactly one Grok account; Cursor bought via the Apple App Store is not auto-cancelled or refunded; enterprise contracts and legacy request-based team plans are not self-serve. Existing subscribers keep their included third-party usage until they switch, and annual subscribers keep their paid term. Team plans add a Cursor Token Rate of $0.25 per MTok for third-party model requests (individuals exempt; Grok and Composer exempt). Worked example: heavy daily Sonnet 5.5 agent use (~3M cached prefix + 200K fresh input + 150K output) costs about $2.20/day, roughly $46/month on top of Premium's $30. The weekly pool size, per-product multipliers, reset day, regional pricing and App Store pricing remain unpublished.

latest_news.title: First public challenge to opaque 'multiplier' quotas: a Kimi top-tier subscriber says old and new same-price tiers disagree
latest_news.summary: An Allegro subscriber on a CNY 6,708/year plan posted that the old tier advertised 10x agent quota while a same-price new Max tier advertises 14x quota and drops the kimi code weekly limit; the poster also noted the old tier's base allowance may have been higher, and asked for a public quantified standard. The real issue is structural: xAI's Plus pool size, Copilot's flex allotment, Zhipu's credit base and Kimi's agent-quota base are all unpublished, so multipliers cannot be checked by users. The only reliable method is to re-run the same real workload on old and new tiers and convert to cost per completed task.

latest_news.title: Codex 28-day challenge: Day 8 global quota reset lands, Day 9 cuts desktop state data 60%
latest_news.summary: Day 8 (announced 10/12 Pacific) was a global quota reset for eligible accounts, applied automatically by end of day; Tibo confirmed 'It's done.' at 13:06 Beijing on 10/13. Day 9 (07:32 Beijing on 10/14) shipped storage optimizations for the ChatGPT and Codex desktop apps that are expected to reduce on-disk state data by 60% - explicitly not RAM, app size, total SSD usage or subscription cost. Day 7 had raised the GPT-6.1 Sol default context in Codex/Work from 272k to 500k. A previously trailed 'materially increase everyone's usage' plan still has no published details.

latest_news.title: DeepSeek pricing reconciled against official docs, and the V4 Pro routing walk-back is confirmed
latest_news.summary: Official docs pricing: V4.1 Flash peak $0.30/$1.20 with cache-hit input $0.003 (off-peak half price); V4 Pro (V4-Pro-0813) peak $1.32/$3.96. Peak is Beijing Mon-Fri 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00; off-peak is half price and all weekend is off-peak. latest_news.title: OpenRouter weekly volume hits a record 172.0T tokens; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash takes first place with 41T
latest_news.summary: For the week ending 10/11, OpenRouter volume reached 172.0 trillion tokens, up 6 trillion (+3.61%) to a new high. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash consumed 41 trillion - more than 3x the second-place GLM-5.3-Flash - helped by routing V4 Pro traffic to it and its very low cache-read cost. GLM-5.3-Flash was second, Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6-Flash third, Step 5 Preview entered at fourth with 8.84 trillion, Tencent Hy4 preview fifth. Claude Opus 5.5 rose five places to 8th and Sonnet 5.5 entered at 15th for the first time since its 9/28 launch. Space Bunny Alpha, Gemini 3.8 Flash and GPT-5.6 Luna all fell back as novelty traffic faded. Open-weight side: MiMo-V2.6-Pro is now the highest-ranked open-weight model on Arena, GLM-5.3 leads at AA index 44.8 / coding 74.8, and Kimi K3's cheapest input price fell 75.7% over ~90 days to $0.730.

latest_news.title: Wholesale token prices keep falling while retail subscriptions rise
latest_news.summary: The global average price per million tokens has fallen below $1, down from $2.05 in May. API cuts are official-level: Anthropic cut Haiku 5.5 input and output by 90%, and OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Luna input from $1 to $0.20 in late July. Meanwhile OpenAI reopened the $200/month Pro in late September at the same price but with per-tier token allowances halved (existing users keep their old allowance only until 10/29), and it sells speed as a separate SKU - GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast at $12/$60 per MTok, 6x standard. Carriers now sell tokens too, at prices ranging from CNY 9.9 to CNY 39.42 for the same 10 million. Takeaway: tokens are priced on cost, subscriptions on value, and the two will not converge soon.

latest_news.title: Alibaba Cloud Bailian: Coding Plan down to Pro only, Token Plan has three hard boundaries

Token Plan rules: you must use the dedicated sk-sp- API key and Base URL (a general Bailian key cannot draw down plan quota); the key is shown in full only once at creation or reset and must not be hardcoded; mixing Token Plan with pay-as-you-go produces unexpected metered charges; and the quota is a 7-day rolling limit, not a calendar-week reset.
