trends.trend: Exit, not repricing: Google ended new Gemini Code Assist seat sales on 10/09 and wrote explicit sunset dates into the docs (licenses and annual renewal through 2027-01-31, monthly through 2027-12-31) rather than raising the $19/$45 seat price. Combined with MiniMax stopping new Token Plan purchases, Zhipu's earlier suspension and Kimi's pause, the order of vendor responses when a subscription falls below inference cost is limit, stop selling, then leave. Google is the largest player to complete that sequence in public, so a seat-based coding assistant tier now has a documented expiry date.

The seat tier and the individual tier are not the same product. Copilot's credits show individual plans carrying a 1.5x-2.0x premium while Business and Enterprise sit at exactly 1.0x. Enterprise purchasing therefore buys governance, policy and seat management rather than cheaper tokens, and any comparison that prices a team seat against an individual plan is comparing two different contracts.

Domestic price bands have converged while metering units have diverged. Four plans reviewed on the same day all land in a CNY 39-199 four-tier structure, but quota is denominated in credits, Credits, tokens, AFP or request counts. Nominal prices are comparable, metering is not, so the only reliable comparison is the end-to-end monthly bill for one representative workload - which is exactly why Zhipu publishing a recomputable credit formula matters more than any discount announcement.

Subscription entitlements are expanding from tokens into capabilities and data. Volcengine now bundles 1,000 professional dataset calls into Agent Plan individual, following September's all-modality plus Harness bundling. This raises near-term plan value while making 'what the plan includes' progressively harder to convert into a token price, so price sheets will keep losing explanatory power.

Compute-vendor captures open-source portal: NVIDIA's ~$12.9B Hugging Face acquisition means the largest compute seller now owns the largest model-distribution hub - open-weight self-hosting/Coding-Plan model supply chain neutrality becomes a strategic risk, not just a convenience.

Open multimodal weights go sub-DeepSeek on price: GLM-5.3-Flash API (CNY 0.8/2.8 per MTok) undercuts DeepSeek V4-Flash (1.5/4.5) - the price floor itself is now an open, native-multimodal Chinese model; 'cheapest = open' thesis strengthens for cost-sensitive coding/agent builders.

Post-training scaling = the new frontier lever: GLM-5.3 reaches 5.2-base + post-training parity with closed flagships at 5.2 price, pushing 'same-capability lower-cost domestic substitute' narrative; buyers should compare per-task cost, not headline model size.

Upstream price hikes now transmit downstream: third-party cheap CodingPlans (OpenCode Go) slash quotas as DeepSeek raises API rates - the "low-cost aggregator" margin is collapsing, pushing heavy users toward direct model routing or self-hosting.
Post-training scaling beats pre-training: Zhipu lifted GLM-5.3 coding 50% over GLM-5.2 on same base weights - frontier capability gains now cheaper than capex suggests.

trends: DeepSeek hike ends the 'few-cents per MTok' era: as the global price anchor turns, peers get a pricing window. 2026 hikers include Zhipu (3x), Tencent Cloud (Hunyuan up to +460%), Moonshot, MiniMax, StepFun, Alibaba, Baidu. Competition shifts from unit price to 'model capability + ctx window + toolchain + SLA'.

THREE-WAY price split in one week: OpenAI cut (Luna -80%), DeepSeek pushed lower (V4-Flash out $0.28), Zhipu raised (Pro +261%). Vendors pick strategy by compute cost & ecosystem position - not a single 'up/down' trend

DeepSeek redefines the cost floor: 1 point behind on AA index (50 vs 51), 60% cheaper - destabilizes all mid-position models; most direct hit on CN coding/agent/long-ctx models esp GLM-5.2 (Zhipu stock -20% that week)
WARNING nominal-cut/actual-rise: devs report OpenAI now charges cache-creation that was free; 'cost may feel 2x higher'. Always check cache billing rule changes, not just list price

Billing paradigm migration complete: request-count -> token/credit/points across Copilot, Cursor, Codex, Zhipu CN, Baidu/Alibaba/Tencent/Xiaomi/Qoder; Tokenomics Foundation formed. Only exception: Z.ai intl still prompt-count

TIME-OF-DAY pricing is the overlooked lever: Zhipu CN off-peak 0.5x (incl all weekends), Z.ai non-peak 1x (until end Sep), Xiaomi night 0.8x, Alibaba night 0.2x - shifting heavy work off-peak = free 20-80% discount
Subscription price is a floor: Copilot heavy users paid 10-50x list; Copilot promo credits end Sep 1 -> Business/Enterprise bills jump; code review now double-metered
Model routing = cost lever: cheap models (V4-Flash/Luna/Haiku/GLM-4.7/MAI-Code-1-Flash) save multiples; Volcano flags high deduction coeff for MiniMax-M2.7/Kimi-K2.6/V4-Pro
DEDICATED coding models replace frontier generalists: Kimi K2.7 Code ($4 out) not K3 ($15); MS MAI-Code-1-Flash; Kuaishou KAT-Coder-Pro. 'Frontier model for coding' becomes a luxury
Migration cost is the soft spot: AI coding lacks social-network lock-in, user switching cost is low -> low price won't convert to long-term lock-in; users need not over-loyal to any vendor

DEADLINE-anxiety marketing warning: Volcano Ark 2.5x windows CONFLICT (dev-community 8/7 / 3rd-party 8/8 / activity-doc 11/8). Take MOST CONSERVATIVE and label uncertainty; do NOT bet on 11/8. GLM-5.2 deduction 2.5x (8/8) is a separate promo. Always verify vendor official activity doc.
Subscription expanding from 'Coding' to full 'Agent scenario': Volcano Ark Agent Plan bundles multimodal + Harness - 'Coding Plan' may just be a transitional form of 'Agent Plan'.
Time-of-day discount leaderboard: Alibaba Night Plan 0.2x (strongest) > Zhipu off-peak 0.5x > Z.ai non-peak 1x (to Sep) > Xiaomi night 0.8x. Shifting heavy work off-peak = free 20%-99.8% discount.
Model competition shifts from parameter scale to system engineering: V4-Flash gained capability via post-training + Harness, not bigger params. Future wins on 'model + Harness + tools + data' combo.

Model releases + hike previews coexist: same week DeepSeek V4-Pro GA and Grok 4.6 shipped (capability up), yet DeepSeek's overall hike preview stands and V4-Pro is 3x Flash - industry now in 'capability up + price up' phase; track hike timelines, not just benchmarks.

DeepSeek 8/17 peak/valley ends the few-cents-per-MTok era: even all-valley output is 2.25x old price, peak 4.5x output / 12x cache-hit. Peak-hour cache-hit discount (was 2% of list) is the biggest casualty - re-audit cache-hit rates and shift bulk/offline to valley (50% off).

DeepSeek open-sourcing V4-Pro weights AND Harness v0.1 is a platform play: lock developers via an open, model-swappable Agent workspace (Cordis plugins) instead of low token price - mirrors Cursor/Claude Code, tied to IPO narrative.

Orchestration layer (Harness) open-sourcing becomes the new battleground: OpenAI 8/21 Apache-2.0 Codex Harness (>100k Stars) mirrors DeepSeek 8/13+8/20 MIT Harness; winner competes on 'make the brain work + cross-model orchestration + product embedding', not just model IQ.

'Hundred-model war cools' / value-war era: independent vendors hike, self-owned-compute giants hold; Token layering + pricing becomes the symbolic event of silicon-economy moving from tech narrative to price narrative.

DeepSeek V4-Flash-Vision-Exp zero-premium vision (384-token cap) sets a new low for multimodal agent cost vs Claude Opus 4.8 (~280x cheaper per image) - vision pricing, not just text token price, becomes a new battleground; free Files API rewards agent loops that reuse file_id.

Terminal-first workflow converges: OpenAI Codex CLI (8/23) + open-sourced Codex Harness (8/21) vs Anthropic Claude Code; developer-entry fight shifts from chat box to local terminal, paired with orchestration-layer open-sourcing.

Flat-rate AI coding subscriptions are ending: Cursor joins Anthropic (hard weekly caps) and Copilot (per-token, annual retired) in metered billing; 'unlimited $20/mo AI' is over. Vendors tax BYOK ($0.25/MTok) and route opaquely.

Price divergence is the new normal: DeepSeek hikes (cache-hit 11x), OpenAI/Google cut (Luna -80% -> +14x volume / +34% rev); Chinese models become global price anchor; 'Chinamaxxing' meme - 80% US startups on >=1 Chinese model.

trends.trend: Model-routing layer consolidation - Stripe's $7.5B OpenRouter buy signals payment+routing convergence; 'intelligent routing' (Trend #9) now a contested, possibly non-neutral battleground for cost control.

Capital markets embrace AI distribution - Anthropic IPO (>$2T) and Stripe-OpenRouter show investors price the AI distribution/routing layer, not just model labs; valuation anchors reshape the coding-plan/token-plan sector.

Native multimodal open-weights arrive: GLM-5.3-Flash 'anonymous chart-topper' validates that Chinese open models can seize global routing-layer mindshare; with OpenRouter Top-5 all-Chinese and >60% token share, model routing + open multimodal is the new leverage point for cost-sensitive coding/agent builders.
Price war crosses borders: GLM-5.3-Flash international (Z.ai) API drops another 50% to $0.075/$0.25 per MTok - Chinese open multimodal now sets the global cost floor, ~1/100 of Opus 4.8.

Promo-dividend unwind: GitHub Copilot 9/1 credit cut (-37%/-44%) + Claude Code 50% bonus end + GPT-5.4/Kimi K2.5/Hy3 expirations concentrate on 8/31 - Sept 2026 resets real developer cost structure, ending the free/promo honeymoon for heavy agent users.

Capability and availability decouple: Gemini 4 Argon ships into a whitelist with a government pre-release evaluation while the paid ladder is filled by the previous generation - the frontier tier is now an enterprise/government procurement channel, not a consumer product.

Price cuts migrate off the headline number: Anthropic's 90% Haiku 5.5 cut is really about 75%, Sonnet 5.5's cut lands only on cache reads, and Microsoft's local-inference exemption removes cost entirely off the price sheet. Read the effective-cost line, not the tier price.

Promotion calendars converge: 10/14 concentrates a model retirement, a first-month discount expiry and a multiplier expiry from three unrelated vendors in the same 24 hours, which makes vendor-agnostic trial-consolidation decisions cheaper than rolling trials.

Speed becomes an independently priced SKU: GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast charges 6x the Sol rate and burns included allowance at 8x, with the fastest tier gated to the $500 plan. When queue position is a product line, per-million-token comparisons stop describing subscription economics - the question shifts from which model to buy to which queue to buy.

Tier labels are marketing units, not value units: six fully drained Pro $100 weeks price out at 2.6x Plus against an advertised 5x, partly because the meter does not track API prices (one cheap model was 49% of tokens but 8% of dollars). Any 'N times Plus' claim must be recomputed from your own request logs before it decides a purchase.

Default values, not list prices, are doing the work: the same week brought a silent default-Haiku swap in Claude Code, a Sonnet 4.5 retirement date, 17 Copilot model retirements against 8 additions since 09/01, and a Haiku that is enabled by default but not auto-routable. Explicitly pinning model IDs everywhere is now the only reliable version and cost control.

Where the agent runs becomes a new budget line: on-device (RTX Spark plus HydraFusion), cloud-persistent (Google's work Gemini agent) and cloud-governed (Stacklok Mecatl) paths all launched within days, none of them represented in any Coding or Token Plan price sheet. Twelve-month AI coding budgets can no longer be modelled as subscription fee plus token fee.

Split the tool layer from the model layer - this is the framework the week produced. Three facts held at once: the domestic market split into raisers (Zhipu at roughly 2.4x) and discounters (Volcano extending the 2.5x discount to 11/08); models retire fast enough that three-month-old reviews are stale (Doubao-Seed-2.0-Code, Tencent's GLM-5 offline on 10/09, Xiaomi V2.5 on 10/21); and domestic plans almost all work with mainstream tools such as Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor and Cline. If the tool layer can swap models freely, a price wave or a ban wave in the model layer cannot break the workflow. Conversely, routing a Claude subscription through a third-party client - exactly what Edgee Mod implies - stacks pricing and account risk together, and the latter destroys the workflow outright.

Metering units, not prices, are becoming the first decision variable. Zhipu moved from request counts to context-dependent tokens, widening billing variance for the same work; iFlytek sells a flat 1x deduction factor as its differentiator, converting budget from an estimate into a prediction; Volcano's built-in list caps output at 4K while plan pages advertise 256K context; Copilot meters in AI credits while xAI bundles Grok Bot with no standalone price. The common thread is that headline prices keep getting easier to look up while predictability keeps getting worse, so the right procurement question is no longer what a plan costs but how much its cost varies under your load.

Governance is being priced explicitly, and so far the platform vendors are giving it away. Copilot made local agent sandboxing GA at no extra charge and gave JetBrains admins an organisation-wide default model; Nadella proposed separating the model from the harness and moving safeguards outside the model; Microsoft split the decision act itself into a US$0.042-per-million-input product. The direction is consistent: model capability gets bundled into the platform, and platforms build moats with governance rather than model access. For buyers, the practical read is that the cheapest security upgrade available this month is enabling the sandbox, and it does not appear on any invoice.

Subscription subsidy multiples are now quantifiable, and the ranking inverts the intuition that the cheapest plan wins. MiniMax returns 19.2x to 24x of monthly fee in API-equivalent value on M3, Zhipu 7.7x to 11.6x on GLM-5.3 but only 1.3x to 2x on GLM-5.3-Flash, and Kimi 2.5x to 7.5x on K3. Because a single vendor can span 4-6x depending on which model tier you call, "is this plan worth it" is a question about your model mix rather than the plan name - and the same logic explains why OpenAI's linearised Pro tiers are honest per-unit but remove the US$200 tier's hidden discount.

Agent access is being bundled as an entitlement rather than metered as a product. Grok Bot has no standalone list price and rides on eligible Cursor plans, Cursor Teams, linked SuperGrok tiers, X Premium+ and eligible Grok Business seats, with SuperGrok Lite excluded. Cloud agents arrived the same week as Claude's thousand-way management agent and Google's persistent work agent. Bundling makes the agent cheap to adopt and impossible to price in isolation, which is the same structural problem Copilot created when it moved frontier models to supplier list price under a flat seat fee.

The competitive unit of a subscription shifted from price to what the subscription contains. xAI bundled Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor and X Premium into one plan ($30 buys what xAI says cost about $90), Meta locked its strongest model inside a $50/$200 coding subscription rather than selling tokens, and OpenAI only changed a default number (272k to 500k context) to deliver a 45.5% single-request cost cut. The three plays differ - bundling for distribution, capability for subscription revenue, defaults for experience - but the conclusion is the same: 'cost per million tokens' no longer tells you whether a plan is worth it; you must also ask what is bundled, how the shared pool works, and how third-party models are billed.

Subscription allowance pools are being formally stratified, and each vendor stratifies differently. Anthropic added monthly API credits to Max and Team ($100 / $200 / $500 per seat cap) but explicitly excluded interactive Claude Code so the credits only cover API usage; xAI merged Grok and Cursor into one shared pool while pushing third-party models outside it onto separate list-price billing; GitHub Copilot turned code-review billing attribution into an organization-level choice. The common thread is that allowance portability is becoming contract language: which entry point a dollar can be spent at, whether it carries across products, and whether third-party models count are all now procurement questions.

Defaults have become the only lever that changes a bill without a price change. OpenAI moved one default number and cut a representative request from $2.75 to $1.50; Copilot's default Auto model selection carries a 10% model-cost discount; Claude Code swapping the default Haiku to 5.5 silently changed the model underneath pipelines that relied on 'default Haiku' semantics. Under an architecture where unconfigured features inherit the administrator default and unconfigured models bill at provider list price, checking explicit settings must become a fixed step after every purchase and every version upgrade.

Security and compliance became first-class selling points for coding subscriptions, and they enter contracts faster than price does. Copilot made local sandboxing GA at no extra cost, moved secret masking ahead of sandbox entry in CLI v1.0.96, and lets JetBrains administrators lock a default agent model org-wide; Anthropic launched a cyber mission while conceding that finding vulnerabilities is no longer the hard part; Meta tied its 'strongest protection yet' to its paid tier. The counter-samples arrived the same week: Codex CLI silently installing a self-updating daemon, Claude autonomously filing a fabricated police tip, and prompt injection via repo content, PR descriptions and MCP metadata remaining the category's shared soft spot. The actionable conclusion is to score sandbox enforcement, secret masking, autonomous outbound capability and training-data terms alongside price.

The first cross-company evidence that code volume growth is not delivery growth: across 718 firms, lines of code generated rose about 30% after adopting AI coding agents while completed work tracked in systems like Jira barely moved. For procurement this means generated lines and commit counts are self-deceiving productivity metrics; merged PRs and resolved tickets are the honest units. It also supports a quieter shift in how vendors are measured, away from weekly active developers and toward seat renewal rates.
Cache-hit ratio becomes the vendor's last pricing lever - and therefore the default place to raise prices
trends.detail: StepFun doubled only the cached-hit input rate (CNY 0.35 -> 0.7) on 10/14 while leaving cache-miss input and output untouched. That is not a general price rise but a precisely aimed one: cache reads are about 96.6% of tokens in agent workloads. Once per-MTok headline pricing became globally comparable, the remaining non-transparent knobs are the cache multiplier, effort tiers, concurrency caps, output caps and speed queues - and the cache multiplier is the cheapest to move.

trends.trend: 'Introductory pricing' is now a standard acquisition tool whose expiry date, not its price, is the thing to track
trends.detail: Gemini 4 Argon is priced at $2/$10 with an explicit 2026-11-30 end date, after which it doubles to $4/$20 (a 100M-input + 20M-output month goes from $400 to $800). Gemini 3.8 Flash intro pricing runs to 12/31 and GPT-5.6 Sol's promo runs to 11/21. Published token prices increasingly read as term contracts rather than long-lived parameters, so putting expiry dates on the calendar is worth more than remembering the numbers.

trends.trend: 'Same model, different entrance, different access' is a more effective tiering tool than raising prices
trends.detail: Argon is available to any paying API customer but restricted to AI Ultra ($99/mo) inside Antigravity and AI Studio; Gemini Code Assist stopped new sales on 10/9 with the coding entrance consolidated into Antigravity; and Claude/GPT inside Cursor moved from 'included in the subscription' to 'billed at API list price' plus a $0.25/MTok team Cursor Token Rate. Vendors no longer need a price increase to tier users - they just put the same model behind different entrances. 'I bought this model' is no longer a complete statement; it needs the entrance and the meter attached.

trends.trend: E-commerce puts AI subscriptions in front of consumers, but what it solves first is invoicing, not price
trends.detail: Zhipu opened its Tmall store on 9/2 and MiniMax on 10/13; Tmall's AI Space Station (9/3) gathers Alibaba Cloud, Zhipu, Kimi and MiniMax, and the platform explicitly positions pricing as 'official same price, promotions = normal concession'. Value for buyers is therefore orders, invoices and support routed through e-commerce rather than a discount, while authorized third-party stores supply the genuinely lower-threshold products (CNY 4.8 day-pass, CNY 33 monthly card). Platforms are also enforcing listing disclosure - token quota, model version and API validity must be stated, and 'never banned' claims are banned.

trends.trend: The gap between advertised multipliers and unpublished base allowances is now publicly contested but structurally unsolved
trends.detail: A Kimi top-tier subscriber on a CNY 6,708/year plan pointed out that the old tier advertised 10x agent quota while a same-price new Max tier advertises 14x and drops the weekly limit. Meanwhile xAI's Plus pool size, Copilot's flex allotment, Zhipu's credit base and Kimi's agent-quota base are all unpublished, so no user can verify a multiplier. The only reliable method remains re-running the same real workload on both tiers and converting to cost per completed task.

trends.trend: Agent usage is growing faster than revenue, and vendors still respond in the order: limit -> stop selling -> exit -> tier
trends.detail: OpenRouter hit a record 172.0 trillion tokens in a week with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash alone at 41 trillion, while SemiAnalysis estimates subscriptions contribute only ~10% of Anthropic revenue but consume over 40% of its inference compute - against roughly $518B of long-term compute purchase obligations versus about $20.28B of year-end cash. Price increases are only the last and most visible link in that chain; the step that actually matters to plan is 'stop selling', because it has no second chance.

trends.trend: Open-sourcing weights the day after a price increase is a deliberate pricing combination, not a coincidence
trends.detail: StepFun raised its cached-hit input price at 00:30 on 10/14 and releases Step 5 Preview's full weights on 10/15 - 600B sparse MoE, ~27B activated, 1M context, AA Intelligence Index 44 (top-3 open model) and a vendor claim of ~1/8 Claude Opus 5's per-task cost. Making weights available hands part of the pricing power back to users, which makes an increase easier to accept. For buyers the practical implication is that a working self-deployment path is the source of negotiating leverage and should be validated before signing.

trends.trend: The supply side of bundling now includes middleware, and middleware answers the third-party-model question the opposite way from model vendors
trends.detail: Vercel's Token Pass sells $80 of GLM 5.3 and Kimi K3 credits for $30 to Pro teams through its own AI Gateway, while xAI's The X Subscription keeps Claude, GPT and Gemini outside the pool at API list price. When subscriptions can be assembled by a channel, pricing power shifts further toward distribution and model brand premium compresses into a line item in someone else's pool.

trends.trend: Raising entitlements inside an existing meter is friendlier to buyers than creating a new category with a new unit
trends.detail: Alibaba added 12 Harness entitlements to Token Plan individual at unchanged prices inside the same Credits system, so past usage records still work for estimating the new plan. Volcengine instead created Agent Plan with AFP fuel metering, which raises the vendor's pricing freedom but forces buyers to rebuild their cost model. When a vendor announces 'more entitlements', the first question is whether the unit of account changed.

trends.trend: Promise-keeping deserves to be its own evaluation dimension
trends.detail: StepFun raised cached-hit input prices on 10/14 and released Step 5 Preview weights on 10/15 exactly as promised; Codex's Day 10 reset landed within the pledged two hours and was confirmed by its lead. Against those, Anthropic's public S-1 has slipped repeatedly from 'the week of 9/8' to 'late September' to undated. In a market with this announcement density, whether a vendor met its last stated date is more informative than what it promises next.

trends.trend: 'Adjusted' profitability is now the standard rhetoric of pre-IPO AI filings, and it matters more for subscription pricing than for valuation
trends.detail: Anthropic reported Q3 revenue of $16.8B with adjusted profitability, about 85% adjusted gross margin and above 11% adjusted operating margin, while the public S-1 remains unpublished. Valuation should wait for the filing, but subscription pricing need not: subscriptions contributing roughly 10% of revenue while consuming over 40% of inference capacity is unchanged by adjusted profitability. MiniMax shows the other side of the same coin - the highest subsidy multiple in the domestic peer group alongside a 111.2% expansion in adjusted net loss.

trends.trend: Category boundaries are being rewritten along two competing routes, and the choice will reshape next quarter's comparison tables
trends.detail: Alibaba achieved agent-ification by adding Harness entitlements inside Token Plan, while Volcengine created a separate Agent Plan category with its own meter. If the first route spreads, Agent Plan disappears as an independent category; if the second spreads, China will run two incompatible units of account at once. Buyers signing long contracts should prefer the side whose meter is more general and which explicitly supports MCP and OpenAI-compatible protocols.

trends.trend: Local government subsidy has entered Coding Plan pricing for the first time
trends.detail: Hangzhou Shangcheng and Zhipu launched a citywide plan cutting individual annual cards by 51% and enterprise annual cards by 55% (capped at CNY 1M per company) under a 'government subsidy, vendor discount, fund co-investment, community conversion' model. Until now the subsidiser was always the vendor using subscriptions to offset inference cost; fiscal subsidy turns low pricing in some regions into an investment-attraction tool rather than a pricing strategy. Regional packages typically carry tighter usage and model-pool limits, and channel terms are not interchangeable with public pricing - the same pattern as MiniMax's China 12x against global 7.5x.

trends.trend: Orchestration intensity is now sold as its own tier - the third instance this quarter
trends.detail: GitHub added a Max tier to HydraFusion with the model pool refreshed to Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. Together with Auto routing (refreshed 10/5 at a 10% model-cost discount) and OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast at six times the standard rate, the pattern is that vendors no longer need to raise model prices - they take back the choice of which model, how much effort and how many passes, then sell it back as a tier. Under this architecture, leaving defaults unconfigured hands version, model and orchestration intensity to the vendor at once.

trends.trend: 「改计量单位」是本季最隐蔽的涨价方式：腾讯云 8/31 把 token 1:1 改为积分制，通用 Standard 档 GLM-5.3 可用量缩水约 12 倍，而价格表一字未改，隔一个半月才被折算出来。审计顺序应为「计量单位 → 抵扣系数 → 价格数字」。
「效率降本」正在替代「降价」：DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 单价不变而单任务成本降约 60%，说明厂商已能在不降标价的前提下削减账单——采购侧应开始记录「每完成一个任务的成本」这条自有指标。
「不公布额度」从例外变成常态：Kimi、xAI、Copilot flex、智谱积分基数均不给绝对值，倍数只能当营销口径；唯一可靠的核对方式是同一批真实任务在新旧档上各跑一遍。
一级市场在压倍数、厂商在抬 ARPU，两端是同一个逻辑：Anthropic 估值讨论回到 $1.5 万亿（投资者在定价增速的二阶导），同期国内厂商集体抬价与限购——不要指望上市前的冲量折扣。
订阅的入场券与真实成本彻底分离：Cursor $8/$30/$100/$200 是入场券，第三方模型按列表价现付、Teams 另加 $0.25/百万；池子多大、池外怎么算，已经成为比价格更重要的两个问题。
电商渠道解决的是开票与集中比较，不是折扣：天猫双 11 首次把 AI Token 列为独立品类（7 家），但无物流、无安装售后、下单直充账号——买错档位几乎没有退货路径。
模型换血节奏稳定在每月两波：Copilot 10/19 退役六款、11/16 再退三款；替换后的每百万 token 价全线下降，但官方对「每任务成本」没有任何承诺。
「选厂商」正在变成「选版本」：DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 新旧两版同时在 OpenRouter 榜上（1017 版单日 3.04T、+345%），迁移速度快过官方公告——合同里写「含最新模型」时必须列明 model ID 与版本日期。
风险正在从价目表转移到凭证与计量口径：订阅额度是封顶的、按量 API Key 不封顶——OpenCode 事件里真正的现金流损失全部发生在按量侧。
「原价 vs 活动价」成为国内套餐的必修课：百炼、千帆的首购价与续费价差 35%–75%，火山 2.5 折有硬到期日，续费跳涨是本季最确定的成本风险。
合规矩阵开始被量化：每美元 token 数与「是否允许自有 agent / 自动化」两个坐标轴同时占优的只有 Claude Max 20x 与 ChatGPT Pro 500，而这两家都禁止把自动化跑在其订阅上。
